Hi,

so the example on 'Unit Fragment Length (UFL) files':

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/unit-fragment-length-ufl-files

does only apply if you have Affymetrix NetAffx
tab-delimited/comma-separated text annotation files. I don't think
that is what you have (below) - correct me if I'm wrong. What is the
source of your annotation file(s)?

Instead, do something similar to what you did for the UGP file, that
is, setup a TabularTextFile and use importFrom() with explicit
specification of argument 'colClassPatterns', e.g.

ufl <- ... (How?)
dat <- TabularTextFile(filename, path=path);
print(dat);

colClassPatterns <- c("^jaxSnpId$"="character",
"^nspiFragmentSize$"="integer", "^styiFragmentSize$"="integer");
colOrder <- c(1,2,3);
units <- importFrom(ufl, dat, colClassPatterns=colClassPatterns,
colOrder=colOrder);

Note that the entries in 'jaxSnpId' (or whatever column you use), must
contain unit names that exist in the CDF, e.g getUnitNames(cdf).

If you have two annotation files, say, one for SNPs and one for CN
probes, you have to do a similar thing for the second file.

Note that you have two enzymes so your UFL maps (unit, fragment length
for enzyme #1, fragment length for enzyme #2). Since unit [indices]
are implicit, your UFL will consist of two columns, one per enzyme.
Did you allocate the UFL that way? It's good if you're explicit
about what your doing.

Does this help?

/Henrik

Hi,

sorry for the delay - I'm on the road. I've checked and I get the
same error using importFrom(ufl, dat, ...) when 'ufl' is an
AromaUflFile. I'll try to fix this bug soon.

In the meanwhile, you can revert to manually assign the values of the
'ufl' file. Below is an example how you can do it. Note that you
have to retrieve the 'unitNames' and the fragment lengths
yourself/manual from your input file. The example does not cover how
to do that, but you can use readDataFrame() for TabularTextFile to do
this conveniently, e.g.

filenameUfl_SNP <- "mDIV.annot.csv";
pathUfl <- "annotationData/chipTypes/mDIV/";
datUfl_SNP <- TabularTextFile(filenameUfl_SNP, path=pathUfl);

colClassPatterns <- c("^Probe ID$"="character", "^NspI Fragment
Size$"="integer", "^StyI Fragment Size$"="integer");
df <- readDataFrame(datUfl_SNP, colClassPatterns=colClassPatterns);

That will read exactly those columns into a data.frame (and nothing
else in case the file is big).

Now to the UFL example...

Example#1 - Manually assign values

cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$byChipType("GenomeWideSNP_6");

# Creates an empty UFL file for this CDF and with two enzymes.
ufl <- AromaUflFile$allocateFromCdf(cdf, tags="HB20091111", nbrOfEnzymes=2);
print(ufl);

first enzyme only.

Hi,

I've provided a patch:

library("aroma.affymetrix");
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

that should make the following work:

units <- importFrom(ufl, dat, colClassPatterns=colClassPatterns,
colOrder=colOrder);

Let me know if work for you (it works here, but I use a in-house
developer's version of aroma.*). If it does, I'll incorporate it in
the package.

/Henrik

>

> tab-delimited/comma-separated text annotation files.  I don't think
> that is what you have (below) - correct me if I'm wrong.  What is the
> source of your annotation file(s)?
>
> Instead, do something similar to what you did for the UGP file, that
> is, setup a TabularTextFile and use importFrom() with explicit
> specification of argument 'colClassPatterns', e.g.
>
> ufl <- ... (How?)
> dat <- TabularTextFile(filename, path=path);
> print(dat);
>
> colClassPatterns <- c("^jaxSnpId$"="character",
>  "^nspiFragmentSize$"="integer", "^styiFragmentSize$"="integer");
> colOrder <- c(1,2,3);
> units <- importFrom(ufl, dat, colClassPatterns=colClassPatterns,
> colOrder=colOrder);
>
> Note that the entries in 'jaxSnpId' (or whatever column you use), must
> contain unit names that exist in the CDF, e.g getUnitNames(cdf).
>
> If you have two annotation files, say, one for SNPs and one for CN
> probes, you have to do a similar thing for the second file.
>
> Note that you have two enzymes so your UFL maps (unit, fragment length
> for enzyme #1, fragment length for enzyme #2).  Since unit [indices]
> are implicit, your UFL will consist of two columns, one per enzyme.
> Did you allocate the UFL that way?   It's good if you're explicit
> about what your doing.
>
> Does this help?
>
> /Henrik
